title: Loss-Guided Density Control and Efficient Backward Optimisation for Compact Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Novel view synthesis based on explicit Gaussian primitives has achieved an effective balance between rendering quality and real-time visualisation, but its training process can remain computationally expensive because adaptive density control may introduce many redundant primitives. This paper proposes an efficient training framework for compact Gaussian Splatting through loss-guided densification, opacity-gradient pruning, and backward-pass optimisation. First, a loss accumulation guided density-control strategy is introduced. Instead of relying only on image-plane gradient magnitude, the method reuses the loss map generated during standard backpropagation to identify persistently under-reconstructed image regions. A binary high-loss mask is accumulated across multiple iterations, and each Gaussian primitive receives a densification score according to its coverage of these regions. Only primitives that consistently contribute to high-error areas are allowed to split or clone, thereby reducing unnecessary growth in well-reconstructed regions. Second, an opacity-gradient-based pruning criterion is designed to remove unstable or low-contribution primitives after densification. By combining opacity, opacity gradients, and training loss over multiple views, the proposed pruning strategy aims to preserve useful primitives while suppressing redundant ones. Third, the CUDA backward pass is optimised through warp-level parallelism and vectorised memory access to reduce redundant global memory transactions. Experiments on Mip-NeRF 360, Deep Blending, and Tanks \& Temples indicate that the proposed framework substantially reduces training time and the final number of Gaussian primitives while maintaining competitive PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS performance compared with representative efficient Gaussian-splatting baselines. The results suggest that loss-aware density control can provide a practical route towards faster and more compact Gaussian Splatting. Our project page is available at https://github.com/Allen-key-20/Loss-Guided-Density-Control-and-Efficient-Backward-Optimisation.git
